make MRJ.jar

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Debugging errors
messages.body_plain:
When I get back NULL from .parseAndEval(), I'd like to gather
information on what went wrong and throw a Java Exception that
contains this information.

I currently just use try() and then check the return value for
try-error class, but that only gives me the error message.  I'm also
interested in getting the traceback.

One idea so far is to either do:

try(
  withCallingHandlers(
    ...,
    error = function(e) {
      e$message <- paste(c(e$message,
capture.output(traceback(sys.calls()[-1:-6]))), collapse='\n')
      signalCondition(e)
    }
  )
)

and then parse the message, searching for and removing the lines
toward the end that fall into the error handling logic.

Are there simpler ways to do this?  Is there any support in REngine for this?

Thanks,

Yang

messages.subject: Re: Debugging errors
messages.body_plain:
On Sep 9, 2011, at 6:57 PM, Yang Zhang wrote:

> When I get back NULL from .parseAndEval(), I'd like to gather
> information on what went wrong and throw a Java Exception that
> contains this information.
> 
> I currently just use try() and then check the return value for
> try-error class, but that only gives me the error message.  I'm also
> interested in getting the traceback.
> 
> One idea so far is to either do:
> 
> try(
>  withCallingHandlers(
>    ...,
>    error = function(e) {
>      e$message <- paste(c(e$message,
> capture.output(traceback(sys.calls()[-1:-6]))), collapse='\n')
>      signalCondition(e)
>    }
>  )
> )
> 
> and then parse the message, searching for and removing the lines
> toward the end that fall into the error handling logic.
> 
> Are there simpler ways to do this?  

Well, the above could be simplified as 

tryCatch(..., error=function(e) { e$trace=unlist(.Traceback); e})

then you can access message, call and trace...


> Is there any support in REngine for this?
> 

Not directly, because REngine only gets exactly the same things you have access to. In addition, R has no low-level facilities for error handling, so you are actually better of using R level tools.

Cheers,
Simon

> <simon.urbanek at r-project.org> wrote:
>>
>> On Sep 9, 2011, at 6:57 PM, Yang Zhang wrote:
>>
>>> When I get back NULL from .parseAndEval(), I'd like to gather
>>> information on what went wrong and throw a Java Exception that
>>> contains this information.
>>>
>>> I currently just use try() and then check the return value for
>>> try-error class, but that only gives me the error message.  I'm also
>>> interested in getting the traceback.
>>>
>>> One idea so far is to either do:
>>>
>>> try(
>>>  withCallingHandlers(
>>>    ...,
>>>    error = function(e) {
>>>      e$message <- paste(c(e$message,
>>> capture.output(traceback(sys.calls()[-1:-6]))), collapse='\n')
>>>      signalCondition(e)
>>>    }
>>>  )
>>> )
>>>
>>> and then parse the message, searching for and removing the lines
>>> toward the end that fall into the error handling logic.
>>>
>>> Are there simpler ways to do this?
>>
>> Well, the above could be simplified as
>>
>> tryCatch(..., error=function(e) { e$trace=unlist(.Traceback); e})
>>
>> then you can access message, call and trace...
>>
>>
>>> Is there any support in REngine for this?
>>>
>>
>> Not directly, because REngine only gets exactly the same things you have access to. In addition, R has no low-level facilities for error handling, so you are actually better of using R level tools.
>>
>> Cheers,
>> Simon
>>
>>
>
>
>
> --
> Yang Zhang
> http://yz.mit.edu/
>



-- 
Yang Zhang
http://yz.mit.edu/
messages.body_snippet:
E.g., at the R shell:

> tryCatch(aoeu, error=function(e) { e$trace = unlist(.Traceback); e })$trace
NULL


> tryCatch(aoeu, error=function(e) { e$trace = capture.output(traceback()); e })$trace
[1] "
